description: FIRST PATTERN-OF-A-CUT GOLDEN (BACKLOG #3 / showcase F1 — pattern could array only a UNION of whole-body copies, so the two most common patterns, bolt-circle mounting holes and lightening-hole rings, could not use it). A 60 x 60 mm square plate sketched on the XY datum, extruded 10 mm into the box [-30,30] x [-30,30] x [0,10]; a SINGLE r4 hole cut through it at (20,0); then a CIRCULAR PATTERN about the world +Z axis through the origin (angle 360 deg, count 6). Because the immediately-preceding body-affecting feature is an extrude-CUT, the pattern arrays that cut's TOOL (option a, docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md 2026-07-13): the seed hole is placement 0 and the tool is reconstructed and REMOVED at placements 1..5 (60/120/180/240/300 deg), so the result is a 6-hole bolt circle — 6 holes REMOVED, not 6 bodies added. A five-feature TREE (sketch -> extrude add -> sketch -> extrude cut -> circular pattern) evaluated through the same evaluate-tree path as every other golden. Locks: the pattern cut-source inference (prev_body_feature is an extrude-cut), the tool reconstruction from the source's already-solved profile, circular_pattern_cut's rotated-tool placement + variadic body.cut + single-solid finalize, GProp over the drilled plate, exact topology after clean(), and (via the parametrized gates) in-process + interpreter-restart byte-determinism and STEP round-trip. The add-pattern path is UNCHANGED and regression-guarded by pattern-circular-4x-quadrant-box / pattern-linear-3x-bar.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Plate: outer square x,y in [-30,30] on XY (4 lines, no constraints -> zero residual, planegcs returns input positions bitwise, same posture as the box/pattern goldens), extruded 10 mm along +Z = the box [-30,30] x [-30,30] x [0,10], volume 60*60*10 = 36000 mm^3.

seed hole: a single r4 circle centred at (20,0), extrude-CUT 10 mm through the full plate depth -> one cylindrical through-hole. The hole is strictly interior (centre 20 from origin + r4 = max reach 24 < 30 half-width) so it does not touch the plate boundary.

pattern: circular, axis through the origin (0,0,0) along +Z, angle 360 deg, count 6 -> step = 360/6 = 60 deg. The source feature is the extrude-cut, so the pattern REPLICATES THAT CUT: placement 0 is the seed hole at (20,0); placements 1..5 are the tool rotated 60/120/180/240/300 deg about +Z, i.e. six holes centred on the bolt circle of radius 20 at angles 0..300 deg. Adjacent hole centres are 2*20*sin(30 deg) = 20 mm apart, r4 each -> 12 mm clearance, so the six holes are mutually disjoint and each is fully interior; the plate stays one connected solid (a cut that severed it would be pattern_disjoint).
volume = 36000 - 6 * (pi * 4^2) * 10 = 36000 - 960*pi = 32984.0710525538 mm^3 (six disjoint cylindrical holes removed, no overlap, so exactly 6x the single-hole removal).

centroid = (0, 0, 5) mm by the 6-fold rotational symmetry of the bolt circle about the +Z axis through the origin (x=y=0) and mid-height (z=5, the holes run the full uniform depth). The axis passes exactly through the centroid in x,y -- a strong check that the 60/120/180/240/300 deg rotations placed the tool copies symmetrically (a biased trig error would pull the centroid off the axis).
bounding_box = [-30,-30,0]..[30,30,10]: the holes are strictly interior, so the AABB is the un-drilled plate's box, unchanged by the cut pattern.

topology: 12 faces (top + bottom plate caps, 4 outer side walls, 6 cylindrical hole walls), 30 edges (top boundary = 4 rect edges + 6 hole circles = 10; bottom = 10; 4 vertical box corner edges; 1 vertical seam edge on each of the 6 periodic hole cylinders = 6), 1 shell. A plate cap bounded by an outer loop + six inner hole loops is still ONE face; the holes add faces/edges only through the six cylinder walls. This generalizes the 2-hole plate golden (8 faces / 18 edges) by +4 cylinder faces and +12 edges (4 more hole circles top+bottom + 4 more seams), proving the pattern cut ran and clean() collapsed the seams (an unmerged cut would show split/extra faces).

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular default, isRelative=False): each full hole circle discretizes to 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1) = 126 segments (the same 2x-angular rule the cylinder/revolve/2-hole-plate goldens exhibit; radius 4 keeps linear deflection non-binding). Six periodic hole cylinders = 6 * ((126+1)*2 nodes, 126*2 tris) = 6 * (254, 252) = 1524 vertices / 1512 triangles. Each plate cap is a planar face with a 4-node rectangular outer loop + six 126-gon holes = 4 + 6*126 = 760 boundary nodes, triangulated with holes to 760 - 2 + 2*6 = 770 triangles (no interior node); two caps = 1520 vertices / 1540 triangles. Four rectangular side walls = 4 * (4 nodes, 2 tris) = 16 vertices / 8 triangles. Totals = 1524 + 1520 + 16 = 3060 vertices and 1512 + 1540 + 8 = 3060 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces — same convention as the box/cylinder/2-hole-plate goldens).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED + ROTATED-CUT tolerance, measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). Unlike the pure-translation linear-pattern golden (deviations EXACTLY 0.0) and the whole-body rotation of pattern-circular-4x-quadrant-box (worst ~1.1e-12), this golden BOTH rotates cylindrical tools by 60/120/180/240/300 deg (non-exact cos/sin) AND boolean-CUTS them through curved walls whose GProp volume/surface use Gauss quadrature, so the residuals compound. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-13, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume |32984.071052553816 - 32984.0710525538| ~ 1.46e-11, surface_area ~ 3.64e-12, centroid.x/.y ~ 5.5e-17 (essentially on-axis), centroid.z exactly 0.0, AABB bounds exactly 0.0. Documented ceiling 1e-8 covers the worst measured residual (~1.46e-11, the volume) with ~690x headroom for libm/BLAS/platform trig variation across CI hosts, while staying 10x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 kernel bound. It is deliberately looser than the 1e-9 of the translation/whole-body-rotation pattern goldens because the rotated curved CUT is a numerically heavier path (measured ~13x their worst residual). Topology and mesh counts carry NO tolerance (exact-match). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
